_readme: One entry per concept. Every concept ships as three slides in this order: definition, visual, how we use it. apply_concepts.py places them; edit here, never in day-decks.json directly.
notes_default: Vaste cadans: definitie → beeld → hoe wij ermee werken. Lees de definitie letterlijk voor, wijs het beeld aan, laat de groep de gebruiksstap zelf zeggen.

definition.title: What is intent.md?
definition.subtitle: The human starting brief: what we want, why it matters, within which boundaries.

cards.title: WHAT
cards.body: The desired result in plain words.

cards.title: WHY
cards.body: The reason, and who is affected.

cards.title: BOUNDARIES
cards.body: Constraints, non-goals and OPEN questions. Unknowns are written down, not guessed.

definition.prompt: Explain: intent.md is the human starting brief for the work, written before design or build. Ask: which three words must always be visible?
steps: Say the three parts: what, why, boundaries.
definition.expected: Everyone can say what intent.md is in one sentence.
definition.check: Everyone names the three parts without looking at the slide.

visual.title: Intent.md in one picture
visual.subtitle: From idea to a shared starting point
visual.imageAlt: intent.md brief with what, why and boundaries feeding design, build and review, with a revisit loop.
visual.imageCaption: What, why and boundaries feed design, build and review. Change the brief before you change the plan.
visual.prompt: Show the picture. Ask participants to link one sentence to what, why or boundaries, and to point at where OPEN questions live.
steps: Link one sentence to the picture.
visual.expected: Everyone can link a sentence to the right part of the brief.
visual.check: Everyone can point at where OPEN questions live in the brief.

usage.title: intent.md · how we use it
usage.subtitle: Written first, read at every gate, changed before the plan changes.

cards.title: BEFORE BUILD
cards.body: Write it in ten minutes: what, why, boundaries. Mark unknowns OPEN. Do not guess.

cards.title: DURING THE WORK
cards.body: The agent reads it first. Every prompt points back to it: "stay inside intent.md".

cards.title: AT REVIEW
cards.body: Review against the brief, not against memory. If the brief was wrong, change the brief, then the plan.

usage.prompt: Walk the three moments. Ask each participant to open their own intent.md and underline one OPEN question before the exercise starts.
steps: Open your intent.md.
Underline one OPEN question.
Say which exercise today uses it.
usage.expected: Every participant has an intent.md with at least one OPEN question.
usage.check: Nobody starts the exercise without an intent.md on screen.

definition.title: What is the evidence rule?
definition.subtitle: A claim counts only with a source, a reproduced check and a reviewer.

cards.title: CLAIM
cards.body: What you say happened, in one sentence.

cards.title: SOURCE + CHECK
cards.body: A row id or file at the cutoff, and the command, calculation or sheet that reproduces it.

cards.title: REVIEWER
cards.body: Someone else reran it. Without all three it is a hypothesis and stays OPEN.

definition.prompt: Read the rule out loud. Ask: what is the difference between a claim and a hypothesis? Ask: why is "it looked right" not evidence?
steps: Name the three parts of evidence.
definition.expected: The room can separate a claim from evidence.
definition.check: Everyone can say why "it looked right" is not evidence.

visual.title: Evidence rule · see the ladder
visual.subtitle: A claim only counts with a source, a reproduced check and a reviewer.
visual.imageAlt: Four steps: claim, source, reproduced check, reviewer; a dashed hypothesis box below; a cutoff stamp.
visual.imageCaption: Claim → source → reproduced check → reviewer. Anything short of that stays a hypothesis and is marked OPEN.
visual.prompt: Walk the four steps left to right. Ask: which step is usually skipped? Let one participant place a claim from the demo on the ladder.
steps: Place one claim from today on the ladder.
visual.expected: Everyone can place a claim on the right step.
visual.check: Everyone can place a claim from today on the right step of the ladder.

usage.title: Evidence rule · how we use it
usage.subtitle: Every result today carries its evidence line or the word OPEN.

cards.title: IN THE EVIDENCE LOG
cards.body: One line per result: claim · source id · command or sheet · reviewer · PASS / FAIL / OPEN.

cards.title: IN THE AGENT'S OUTPUT
cards.body: Ask for source ids and the check in the answer. No source, no claim.

cards.title: AT THE HUMAN GATE
cards.body: The reviewer reruns one check before accepting. Unrun checks stay OPEN, never "probably fine".

usage.prompt: Open the evidence log template. Write one evidence line for the demo result together, then let everyone mark one thing OPEN on purpose.
steps: Open the evidence log template.
Write one evidence line for the demo result.
Mark one thing OPEN on purpose.
usage.expected: Everyone has written one complete evidence line.
usage.check: No evidence line is missing a source or a reviewer.

definition.title: What is MOB programming?
definition.subtitle: One task, one screen, one human driver; the group navigates and rotates.

cards.title: GROUP
cards.body: 3–4 people on one shared task and one screen.

cards.title: ROLES
cards.body: Driver types, navigator directs, skeptic asks for source ids, scribe records the decision. Rotate every 5–7 minutes.

cards.title: AI IN THE MOB
cards.body: The tool suggests. Humans direct, say "pause" on uncertainty, and decide.

definition.prompt: Demonstrate a two-minute mob: facilitator states the task, one navigator directs the human driver, the skeptic asks for source ids, the scribe records the decision. Rotate the driver once.
steps: Name the four roles.
Say the pause rule.
definition.expected: The room can name the roles and the pause rule.
definition.check: Participants can name driver, navigator, skeptic and scribe.

visual.title: MOB programming · see the roles
visual.subtitle: One laptop, one screen, everyone in a role; rotate every five to seven minutes.
visual.imageAlt: Four roles on one chain: driver, navigator, skeptic, scribe, with a rotate-every-5-to-7-minutes callout and one shared laptop.
visual.imageCaption: Driver types what the navigator says. Skeptic asks for source ids, scribe records the decision. A human decides at every gate.
visual.prompt: Point at each role. Ask: who is driver first, who calls the rotation, and who says "pause" first?
steps: Name your first driver and navigator.
visual.expected: Every group can point at its four roles.
visual.check: Everyone can say who asks for source ids and who records the decision.

usage.title: MOB programming · how we use it
usage.subtitle: Every guided exercise today runs as a mob with a visible timer.

cards.title: START
cards.body: Facilitator states one task. First driver and navigator are named before the timer starts.

cards.title: ROTATE
cards.body: Every 5–7 minutes the driver changes. Remote participants rotate too; the navigator reads chat aloud.

cards.title: PAUSE
cards.body: Anyone says "pause" when a source, assumption or claim is unclear. The scribe records the decision.

usage.prompt: Let each group name its first driver and navigator, set the rotation timer, and agree who says "pause" first. Do not start the exercise before that.
steps: Name your first driver and navigator.
Set the rotation timer.
Agree who says "pause" first.
usage.expected: Every group has named roles before the first exercise.
usage.check: No group starts an exercise without a named driver and a running timer.

definition.title: What is an AI-native SDLC?
definition.subtitle: The same control objectives, new enforcement: the line becomes a loop and AI is embedded at every point.

cards.title: FROM LINE TO LOOP
cards.body: Plan → Design → Build → Test → Deploy → Maintain, and what production teaches re-enters the plan.

cards.title: AI AT EVERY POINT
cards.body: AI drafts, generates, reviews first, tests and watches. Humans set intent, judge risk and own the release.

cards.title: SAME CONTROLS, NEW ENFORCEMENT
cards.body: Quality, security and traceability stay. They move from checklists and sign-offs into the pipeline, with automated handover between plays.

definition.prompt: Read the definition out loud, word for word. Ask: which control objective changed? (None.) Ask: what changed? (The shape, the handover, the enforcement.)
steps: Name the six phases.
Name one control objective that did not change.
definition.expected: The room can say "same objectives, new enforcement" and explain it.
definition.check: Everyone can name the six phases and one unchanged control objective.

visual.title: AI-native SDLC · see the loop
visual.subtitle: The line becomes a repeatable loop with AI at every point.
visual.imageAlt: Six phase pills on one orange loop: plan, design, build, test, deploy, maintain, with Claude in the centre helping at every point.
visual.imageCaption: Six phases on one repeating loop with Claude at every point. Intent, review and release remain human decisions.
visual.prompt: Use the picture to point at the loop. Then let participants place their own ticket on one phase and point at one human gate.
steps: Point at the loop. Place your ticket.
visual.expected: Everyone has placed a real ticket on one phase.
visual.check: Everyone can point at the phase their ticket is in and at one human gate.

usage.title: AI-native SDLC · how we use it
usage.subtitle: Per phase: what the AI does first, what the engineer decides.

columns.title: AI's role
items: Plan · drafts the spec, sizes the work, flags dependencies
Design · proposes options against the spec
Build · generates and refactors; first-pass review on every change
Test · writes, runs and maintains the suite
Deploy · checks the gates and triggers the release
Maintain · watches, triages and files the follow-up

columns.title: The engineer's role
items: Plan · sets intent and priorities
Design · decides design and risk
Build · directs, constrains, accepts
Test · defines what correct means
Deploy · owns the rollback decision
Maintain · handles what AI escalates

usage.prompt: Walk the six rows. For each phase, name the AI's first pass and the decision that stays human. Then let everyone map one real ticket to a phase and a human decision.
steps: Pick your ticket's phase.
Say the AI's first pass for it.
Say the decision that stays yours.
usage.expected: Every participant has mapped one real ticket to a phase and a human decision.
usage.check: Nobody names a phase where the human has no decision.

definition.title: What is an agent?
definition.subtitle: A model in a loop with a goal, tools, feedback, authority and memory. The model matters; the loop turns language into work.

items.label: Feedback
items.caption: tool results feed the next step

definition.tagline: DEBUG THE SYSTEM — NOT THE MYTH
definition.prompt: Say one sentence per pillar. A model predicts text. Give it a goal, tools, feedback and a boundary and it becomes an agent. A subagent is an agent another agent delegates to, with its own context.
steps: Say model, chat, agent, subagent in one sentence each.
definition.expected: The room can say model, chat, agent, subagent in one sentence each.
definition.check: Nobody calls the model itself the agent.

visual.title: The agentic loop · see the loop
visual.subtitle: Gather context → take action → verify results, repeat until done, interrupt at any point.
visual.imageAlt: Your prompt enters a loop of gather, act and verify that repeats until done; a human box can interrupt, steer or add context at any point.
visual.imageCaption: Models reason, tools act, the harness holds the loop. The loop ends at a human gate, never at "done" by itself.
visual.prompt: Point at the three phases, the repeat arrow and the human interrupt. Map each phase to this morning's ticket-coach: read the ticket, draft the packet, check against the contract.
steps: Point at the three phases and the human interrupt.
visual.expected: Everyone can point at gather, act, verify and the interrupt.
visual.check: Everyone can point at the three phases, the repeat and the human interrupt.

usage.title: The agentic loop · how we use it
usage.subtitle: Read the trace, not the prose: each loop turn leaves a tool call you can check.

cards.title: BOUND THE TASK
cards.body: One ticket, one contract, one boundary in the prompt. The agent must be able to stop.

cards.title: WATCH THE LOOP
cards.body: n8n shows execution steps; Claude Code shows tool calls. A Calculator or Read call is an action. Reasoning alone is not.

cards.title: INTERRUPT ON PURPOSE
cards.body: Steer, add context or stop when the loop drifts. The loop ends at a human gate.

usage.prompt: Open the demo trace. Let everyone point at one real tool call, name the boundary in the prompt, and say where they would interrupt.
steps: Point at one real tool call in the demo trace.
Name the boundary in the prompt.
Say where you would interrupt.
usage.expected: Everyone can find one tool call in a trace.
usage.check: No one claims a result the trace does not show.

definition.title: What is "one contract, two platforms"?
definition.subtitle: Same functional contract and input on n8n and Claude Code; only the harness and its adapter differ.

cards.title: THE CONTRACT
cards.body: shared-prompt.md and the ticket input: what the agent must produce and must not do.

cards.title: THE ADAPTERS
cards.body: n8n: system message, model, Calculator tool. Claude Code: subagent body, read-only tools, typed invocation. Recorded per platform.

cards.title: THE CHECKER
cards.body: Both outputs go through the same checker. Differences are observations; one pair of runs proves no cause.

definition.prompt: Show shared-prompt.md and TICKET-OPS-101. In n8n the contract is the AI Agent system message and the ticket is the user message, with Calculator as the tool adapter. In Claude Code it is the ticket-coach subagent body with read-only Read, Glob and Grep plus the typed invocation.
steps: Say where the instruction lives on each platform.
definition.expected: Everyone knows where the instruction lives on each platform.
definition.check: Everyone can name the contract and one adapter setting per platform.

visual.title: One contract · see the split
visual.subtitle: Same contract and input; only the harness and its adapter differ.
visual.imageAlt: One contract box feeding n8n and Claude Code boxes, both feeding the same checker.
visual.imageCaption: One contract feeds two harnesses; both outputs go through the same checker. One pair of runs proves no cause.
visual.prompt: Point at the contract, then at both adapters, then at the checker. Ask: what is shared, what is recorded separately?
steps: Name the adapter settings you will record.
visual.expected: Everyone can say what is shared and what differs.
visual.check: Everyone can point at what is shared and what is recorded separately.

usage.title: One contract · how we use it
usage.subtitle: Morning n8n, afternoon Claude Code, same ticket, same checker, settings recorded.

columns.title: n8n · morning
items: Manual trigger → Set node with the ticket
AI Agent: system message = shared functional contract
Anthropic Chat Model (Claude Sonnet 5)
Calculator via ai_tool
Execution view shows intermediate steps

columns.title: Claude Code · afternoon
items: ticket-coach subagent = shared functional contract
Read / Glob / Grep read-only tools on the same files
Typed invocation from the lab README
Preview in chat, checker after
Transcript shows logged successful tool calls

usage.prompt: Record each platform's adapter instructions, model, mode, access and tools; the board prompt is a summary, not a third instruction. Only after the human gate move to ticket 102: the contract travels, the adapter is rebuilt.
steps: Copy the adapter settings table.
Fill it for the platform you are on.
Mark unrun checks OPEN.
usage.expected: Every participant has a filled adapter settings line for one platform.
usage.check: No comparison sentence claims a cause from one pair of runs.

definition.title: What is a human gate?
definition.subtitle: The point where the agent's output waits for a human decision: accept, or return with a named reason.

cards.title: WHAT WAITS
cards.body: A draft, a preview, a trace and its evidence line. Nothing has been written to a business system.

cards.title: WHO DECIDES
cards.body: A named human who reruns one check and decides PASS, FAIL or OPEN.

cards.title: WHAT RETURNS
cards.body: A returned result names the gap. Nothing is "probably fine".

definition.prompt: Explain the gate with today's baseline: settings, output, review line, decision. Ask: what would make you return it?
steps: Say what waits at the gate and who decides.
definition.expected: The room can describe a gate in one sentence.
definition.check: Everyone can name the three outcomes PASS, FAIL, OPEN and what each requires.

visual.title: Human gate · see the decision
visual.subtitle: The agent proposes; a human accepts or returns with a named reason.
visual.imageAlt: Agent output enters a gate where a human reviews the evidence, then accept or return; a dashed arrow returns to the agent.
visual.imageCaption: Nothing is written to a business system without this decision. Return always names the gap.
visual.prompt: Trace the arrows. Ask: what must the reviewer see before accepting? What travels back on the return arrow?
steps: Say what your gate needs: source, check, reviewer.
visual.expected: Everyone can trace accept and return.
visual.check: Everyone can trace the return arrow and say what it carries.

usage.title: Human gate · how we use it
usage.subtitle: Every practice block ends at a gate before anything moves on.

cards.title: BEFORE THE GATE
cards.body: Freeze the baseline: settings, output, review line per person.

cards.title: AT THE GATE
cards.body: The reviewer reruns one check and decides with one quoted line as the reason.

cards.title: AFTER THE GATE
cards.body: PASS moves to the next ticket, FAIL returns with the gap named, OPEN stays visible on the board.

usage.prompt: Each person writes a review line and decides PASS / FAIL / OPEN with one quoted line. OPEN items go on the board before anyone moves on.
steps: Write your review line.
Decide PASS / FAIL / OPEN with one quoted line.
Put OPEN items on the board.
usage.expected: A decision per participant with a quoted reason.
usage.check: No decision claims an unobserved run.
